title: Chris Kelly's audiences
summary: They discuss whether Kelly played for rougher crowds or society dates; Howard says he played many white dances and everywhere else.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Chris Kelly, the blues trumpeter and his band

blocks.x: Some people told me that Chris mostly played like you might say for a rougher crowd, not the society dates so much. Is that true?
I think that his followers mostly the common people you might say rather than the dicky and ritzy people.

Well no, I don't think he made connection that kind of way because they kept him so busy with those kind of people which you may see. And other words, money, money, and he first come for his soil. Yeah. You see.
He played all sorts of dances.
He played a lot of white dances.
I don't mean necessarily white but I mean color to the woman. I mean like say the Fronson Me Hall. You know, sort of a classic place where they didn't have much rough music or music.
Well I don't know about him playing at the Fronson Me Hall or different places but I know he played all in other places. I know that for sure.
